text:
alex: Getting a straggler AccessDenied after rotating the CMK used for envelope encryption. Lambda that reads S3 objects fails intermittently with kms:Decrypt. Started after rotation + rekeying.
mira: ugh. do you have the exact error? sometimes grant tokens or assumed role session policies bite us.
alex: logs show this in CloudWatch:
```
AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::111122223333:assumed-role/data-reader/ci-session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111122223333:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789
```
It looks like the lambda assumes role `data-reader` which is allowed in IAM, but after rotation some decrypts succeed and some fail.
raj: did we rotate with Grant tokens or did we re-encrypt S3 objects with a new key id? Grants are ephemeral and can be revoked on rotation.
alex: We rotated the CMK and created a new key. We left the old key enabled for a few hours. There was also an automatic rewrap job that re-encrypted newer objects to the new key.
mira: Check CloudTrail for `kms:CreateGrant` and `kms:RevokeGrant` around the rotation time. If a grant was created for the old key and then revoked mid-flight, any in-flight decrypt using a grant token could fail.
jen: Also confirm the Lambda execution role is calling KMS with the right encryptionContext. Envelope encryption often uses an `x-amz-cek` flow; mismatch in EncryptionContext will lead to AccessDenied too.
alex: Good call. CloudTrail shows: `RevokeGrant` for grantId `g-1234` at 2024-04-12T18:02:31Z, and there are `Decrypt` attempts between 18:02:28Z and 18:02:33Z.
raj: that matches an in-flight request window. If the decrypt used a grant token returned earlier, but the grant got revoked before KMS processed it, you'd see intermittent failures.
mira: For future rotations, best practice: 1) pause rewrap or traffic, 2) rotate key, 3) create grants on the new key for roles, 4) wait for propagation, 5) flip rewrap or traffic. Also consider using key policy changes instead of grants if you need persistent role access.
alex: Quick workaround—retry on kms:Decrypt failures for a few seconds. The requests that failed and retried succeeded once the grant/token state stabilized.
jen: Can you paste the relevant parts of the key policy? we should ensure the new key policy explicitly allows the `data-reader` assumed-role principal or the AWS account root.
alex: Snippet from the new key policy:
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Sid": "Allow use by data-reader",
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/data-reader"},
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:DescribeKey"],
      "Resource": "*"
    }
  ]
}
```
raj: That looks fine, but remember lambda runs as an assumed role session: the principal in KMS key policy must match the role's ARN, not the assumed-role session ARN. Here you used the role ARN, so OK. But if the caller used an AWS service principal or cross-account assume-role, you may need `kms:ViaService` statements.
mira: Also check for any session policy or STS session boundary applied during assume-role. A session policy can remove kms:Decrypt even if the role has it.
alex: We do have a session policy in the CI pipeline that restricts some actions. I'll check session policy logs.
jen: Another angle: when using grants from a service (like S3 or a Kinesis connector), grant tokens are passed around. If rotation revoked the grant and you rewrapped, earlier-created grant tokens are invalid. Consider granting decrypt to the service principal (eg `kms:ViaService`) for transitional window.
alex: Action items: 1) confirm CloudTrail lines for CreateGrant/RevokeGrant, 2) confirm no restrictive session policy applied at assume time, 3) add short retry logic around kms:Decrypt, 4) update rotation playbook to create grants on new key before revoking old grants.
mira: Also add an alert in Console that flags a spike in kms:Decrypt AccessDenied errors during rotations.
deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback not required — mitigation in place (retries) — monitoring alerted.
raj: One extra note: if you use EnvelopeKey stored in a database and rewrapped to the new CMK, ensure the rewrap job attaches the same EncryptionContext used originally, otherwise KMS will reject with AccessDenied.
alex: thanks all. I'll file a postmortem draft and update the rotation runbook.
jen: TL;DR: intermittent AccessDenied post-rotation likely from revoked grants / grant-token race + possible session policy mismatch. Fixes: add grant-to-new-key before revoke, validate session policies, and retry decrypts for short window. :thumbsup:
